text: If the coefficient of $x^{7}$ in $\left (ax^{2}+\frac{1}{2bx}\right )^{11}$ and $x^{-7}$ in $\left (ax-\frac{1}{3bx^{2}}\right )^{11}$ are equal, then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
General term of $\left (ax^{2}+\frac{1}{2bx}\right )^{11}$ is

$T_{r+1}={}^{11}C_{r}\left (ax^{2}\right )^{11-r}\left (\frac{1}{2bx}\right )^{r}={}^{11}C_{r}(a)^{11-r}\left (\frac{1}{2b}\right )^{r}x^{22-3r}$

$\begin{array}{ll}  & \text{Now,}22-3r=7 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow 15=3r \\  \\  & \Rightarrow r=5 \end{array}$

and general term of $\left (ax-\frac{1}{3bx^{2}}\right )^{11}$ is

$\begin{array}{ll} T_{r+1} & ={}^{11}C_{r}(ax)^{11-r}\left (-\dfrac{1}{3bx^{2}}\right )^{r} \\  \\ ={}^{11}C_{r}a^{11-r}\left (-\dfrac{1}{3b}\right )^{r}x^{11-3r} \end{array}$

Now, $11-3r=-7$

$\Rightarrow 18=3r\Rightarrow r=6$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Since, coefficient of}x^{7}\text{in}\left (ax^{2}+\dfrac{1}{2bx}\right )^{11} \\  \\ =\text{Coefficient of}x^{-7}\text{in}\left (ax-\dfrac{1}{3bx^{2}}\right )^{11} \\  \\ \Rightarrow {}^{11}C_{5}(a)^{6}\left (\dfrac{1}{2b}\right )^{5}={}^{11}C_{6}(a)^{5}\left (-\dfrac{1}{3b}\right )^{6} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{a}{32b^{5}}=\dfrac{1}{729b^{6}}\Rightarrow 729ab=32 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text: Let $a\neq b$ be two non-zero real numbers. Then the number of elements in the set $X=\left \{z\in \mathrm{ℂ}:\mathrm{Re}\left (az^{2}+bz\right )=a \right.$ and $\left. \mathrm{Re}\left (bz^{2}+az\right )=b\right \}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $z=x+iy$

$\begin{array}{ll}  & \Rightarrow z^{2}=x^{2}-y^{2}+2ixy \\  \\  & \therefore az^{2}+bz \\  \\  & =a\left (x^{2}-y^{2}+2ixy\right )+b(x+iy) \\  \\  & =a\left (x^{2}-y^{2}\right )+bx+2aixy+biy \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{Re}\left (az^{2}+bz\right )=a \\  \\ \Rightarrow a\left (x^{2}-y^{2}\right )+bx=a \\  \\ \Rightarrow x^{2}-y^{2}+\frac{b}{a}x=1.........(i) \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{and}bz^{2}+az \\  \\ =b\left (x^{2}-y^{2}+2ixy\right )+a(x+iy) \\  \\ =b\left (x^{2}-y^{2}\right )+ax+2bixy+aiy \\  \\ \mathrm{Re}\left (bz^{2}+az\right )=b \\  \\ \Rightarrow b\left (x^{2}-y^{2}\right )+ax=b \\  \\ \Rightarrow x^{2}-y^{2}+\dfrac{a}{b}x=1..........(ii) \end{array}$

On subtracting Equation (ii) from Equation (i), we get

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{b}{a}x-\dfrac{a}{b}x=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \left (\dfrac{b}{a}-\dfrac{a}{b}\right )x=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow x=0\text{or}\dfrac{b}{a}-\dfrac{a}{b}=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow b^{2}-a^{2}=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow a=\pm b \\  \\ \Rightarrow a=-b(\text{since}a\neq b) \end{array}$

From (i), when $x=0$, then

$\begin{array}{l} 0-y^{2}=1\Rightarrow y^{2}=-1 \\  \\ \Rightarrow y\in 𝜙\Rightarrow z\in 𝜙\text{has no solution.} \end{array}$

When, $a=-b$, then $x^{2}-y^{2}-x=1$ has infinitely many solutions.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text: Let $P$ be a square matrix such that $P^{2}=I-P$. For $α,β,γ,δ\in \mathrm{ℕ}$, if $P^{α}+P^{β}=γI-29P$ and $P^{α}-P^{β}=δI-13P$, then $α+β+γ-δ$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We have, $P^{2}=I-P$

$\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow P^{4} & =(I-P)^{2}=I+P^{2}-2P \\  \\ =2I-3P\text{[Using Eq. (i)]} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow P^{8} & =(2I-3P)^{2} \\  \\ =4I+9P^{2}-12P \\  \\ =13I-21P\text{[Using Eq. (i)]} \end{array}$

and

$\begin{array}{ll} P^{6} & =(I-P)(2I-3P) \\  \\ =2I-3P-2P+3P^{2} \\  \\ =5I-8P\text{[Using Eq. (i)]} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Now,}P^{8}+P^{6}=18I-29P \\  \\ \text{and}P^{8}-P^{6}=8I-13P \\  \\ \therefore α=8,β=6,γ=18,δ=8 \\  \\ \therefore α+β+γ-δ=8+6+18-8=24 \end{array}$

text:
If the solution curve $f(x,y)=0$ of the differential equation 

$(1+\log _{e}x)\frac{dx}{dy}-x\log _{e}x=e^{y},x>0$, 

passes through the points $(1,0)$ and $(α,2)$, then $α^{α}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Put $t=x\log _{e}x$; then $\dfrac{dt}{dy}=(1+\log _{e}x)\dfrac{dx}{dy}$, and the equation becomes

$\dfrac{dt}{dy}-t=e^{y}$

With integrating factor $e^{-y}$:

$t~e^{-y}=\int e^{y}e^{-y}dy=y+c\Rightarrow x\log _{e}x=(y+c)e^{y}$

At $(1,0)$: $0=c$, so $x\log _{e}x=ye^{y}$.

At $(α,2)$: $α\log _{e}α=2e^{2}$, i.e. $\log _{e}α^{α}=2e^{2}$, so $α^{α}=e^{2e^{2}}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text: Let $f(x)$ be a function satisfying $f(x)+f(π-x)=π^{2},\forall x\in \mathrm{ℝ}$. Then $\int\limits _{0}^{π}f(x)\sin xdx$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $I=\int\limits _{0}^{π}f(x)\sin xdx$ ..........(i)

$\begin{array}{l} =\int\limits _{0}^{π}f(π-x)\sin (π-x)dx \\  \\ =\int\limits _{0}^{π}f(π-x)\sin xdx........(ii) \end{array}$

On adding Equations (i) and (ii), we get

$\begin{array}{l} 2I=\int\limits _{0}^{π}[f(x)+f(π-x)]\sin xdx \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2I=\int\limits _{0}^{π}π^{2}\sin xdx=π^{2}\int\limits _{0}^{π}\sin xdx \\  \\ =π^{2}(-\cos x)_{0}^{π}=-π^{2}(-1-1)=2π^{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow I=π^{2} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text: $\lim _{n\to \infty }\left \{\left (2^{\frac{1}{2}}-2^{\frac{1}{3}}\right )\left (2^{\frac{1}{2}}-2^{\frac{1}{5}}\right )\ldots ..\left (2^{\frac{1}{2}}-2^{\frac{1}{2n+1}}\right )\right \}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $L=\lim _{n\to \infty }\left \{\left (2^{\frac{1}{2}}-2^{\frac{1}{3}}\right )\left (2^{\frac{1}{2}}-2^{\frac{1}{5}}\right )\ldots \left (2^{\frac{1}{2}}-2^{\frac{1}{2n+1}}\right )\right \}$ 

Here, $\left (2^{\frac{1}{2}}-2^{\frac{1}{3}}\right )^{n}<\left (2^{\frac{1}{2}}-2^{\frac{1}{3}}\right )\left (2^{\frac{1}{2}}-2^{\frac{1}{5}}\right )$
$\ldots \left (2^{\frac{1}{2}}-2^{\frac{1}{2n+1}}\right )<\left (2^{\frac{1}{2}}-2^{\frac{1}{2n+1}}\right )^{n}$

$\Rightarrow \lim _{n\to \infty }\left (2^{\frac{1}{2}}-2^{\frac{1}{3}}\right )^{n}<L<\lim _{n\to \infty }\left (2^{\frac{1}{2}}-2^{\frac{1}{2n+1}}\right )^{n}$

Since, $\lim _{n\to \infty }\left (2^{\frac{1}{2}}-2^{\frac{1}{3}}\right )^{n}=0$ and $\lim _{n\to \infty }\left (2^{\frac{1}{2}}-2^{\frac{1}{2n+1}}\right )^{n}=0$

$\therefore L=0$

text: In a group of 100 persons 75 speak English and 40 speak Hindi. Each person speaks at least one of the two languages. If the number of persons, who speak only English is $α$ and the number of persons who speak only Hindi is $β$, then the eccentricity of the ellipse $25\left (β^{2}x^{2}+α^{2}y^{2}\right )=α^{2}β^{2}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $E$ be the person speak, English

$\therefore n(E)=75$

and $H$ be the person speak Hindi

$\therefore n(H)=40$

Let number of persons who speak both English and Hindi are $t$.


[IMG]


$\begin{array}{ll}  & \therefore α+t+β=100........(i) \\  \\  & α+t=75........(ii) \\  \\  & \text{and}β+t=40........(iii) \end{array}$

From Equations (i) and (ii), $β=25$

From Equations (i) and (iii), $α=60$ and from Eq. (i), $t=15$

We have, equation of ellipse

$\begin{array}{ll} 25\left (β^{2}x^{2}+α^{2}y^{2}\right ) & =α^{2}β^{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 25\left (\dfrac{x^{2}}{α^{2}}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{β^{2}}\right ) & =1 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 25\left (\dfrac{x^{2}}{3600}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{625}\right )=1 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{x^{2}}{144}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{25}=1 \\  \\ \therefore \text{Eccentricity,}e=\sqrt{1-\dfrac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}}=\sqrt{1-\dfrac{25}{144}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{119}}{12} \end{array}$

text: Three dice are rolled. If the probability of getting different numbers on the three dice is $\frac{p}{q}$, where $p$ and $q$ are co-prime, then $q-p$ is equal to :

solution.body:
Total number of outcomes $=6\times 6\times 6=216$

Number of outcomes getting different numbers on the three dice are ${}^{6}P_{3}=\frac{6!}{3!}=120$

$\therefore$ Required probability $=\frac{120}{216}=\frac{5}{9}$

$\therefore p=5$ and $q=9$

$\therefore q-p=9-5=4$

text:
For the system of equations

$x+y+z=6$

$x+2y+αz=10$

$x+3y+5z=β$, which one of the following is NOT true?
options: System has a unique solution for $α=3,β\neq 14$.
System has infinitely many solutions for $α=3,β=14$.
System has a unique solution for $α=-3,β=14$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given system of equations,

$\begin{array}{ll} x+y+z & =6........(i) \\  \\ x+2y+αz & =10........(ii) \\  \\ x+3y+5z & =β........(iii) \end{array}$

Here, 

$\begin{array}{llllllll} \Delta  & =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & α \\ 1 & 3 & 5 \end{array}\right | \\  \\ =1(10-3α)-1(5-α)+1(3-2) \\  \\ =10-3α-5+α+1 \\  \\ =6-2α \end{array}$

For unique solution, $\Delta \neq 0$

$\Rightarrow 6-2α\neq 0\Rightarrow α\neq 3$

When, $α=3$

$\begin{array}{llllllll} \Delta _{1} & =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 6 & 1 & 1 \\ 10 & 2 & 3 \\ β & 3 & 5 \end{array}\right | \\  \\ =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 \\ β-18 & 3 & 2 \end{array}\right |=-1(-4-β+18) \\  \\ =β-14 \end{array}$

and 

$\begin{array}{llllllll} \Delta _{2} & =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 1 & 10 & 3 \\ 1 & β & 5 \end{array}\right | \\  \\ =1(50-3β)-6(5-3)+1(β-10) \\  \\ =50-3β-12+β-10 \\  \\ =28-2β=2(14-β) \end{array}$

and

$\begin{array}{llllllll} \Delta _{3} & =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 2 & 10 \\ 1 & 3 & β \end{array}\right | \\ =1(2β-30)-1(β-10)+6(3-2) \\  \\ =2β-30-β+10+6 \\  \\ =β-14 \end{array}$

Thus, at $β=14,\Delta _{1}=\Delta _{2}=\Delta _{3}=0$

$\Rightarrow α=3,β=14$

So, for $α=3,β=14$ the system has infinitely many solutions (option B is true), and for $α=3,β\neq 14$ (e.g. $β=24$) it has no solution (option C is true).

For $α=-3$, $\Delta =6+6=12\neq 0$, so the system has a unique solution (option D is true).

For $α=3$, $\Delta =0$, so the system can never have a unique solution. Hence the statement in option A is NOT true, and the answer is option A.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text:
Let the sets A and B denote the domain and range respectively of the function $f(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{⌈x⌉-x}}$, where $⌈x⌉$ denotes the smallest integer greater than or equal to $x$. Then among the statements

(S1) : $A\cap B=(1,\infty )-\mathrm{ℕ}$ and

(S2) : $A\cup B=(1,\infty )$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{⌈x⌉-x}}$

If $\mathrm{x}\in \mathrm{I},⌈\mathrm{x}⌉=[\mathrm{x}]$ (greatest integer function)

If $x\notin I,⌈x⌉=[x]+1$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\left \{\begin{array}{l} \frac{1}{\sqrt{[\mathrm{x}]-\mathrm{x}}},\mathrm{x}\in \mathrm{I} \\  \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{[\mathrm{x}]+1-\mathrm{x}}},\mathrm{x}\notin \mathrm{I} \end{array} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\left \{\begin{array}{l} \frac{1}{\sqrt{-\{\mathrm{x}\}}},\mathrm{x}\in \mathrm{I},\text{(does not exist)} \\  \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-\{\mathrm{x}\}}},\mathrm{x}\notin \mathrm{I} \end{array} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \text{domain of}\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{I} \end{array} \right.  \right.$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Now,}\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-\{\mathrm{x}\}}},\mathrm{x}\notin \mathrm{I} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 0<\{\mathrm{x}\}<1 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 0<\sqrt{1-\{\mathrm{x}\}}<1 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-\{\mathrm{x}\}}}>1 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \text{Range}=(1,\infty ) \\  \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{A}=\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{I} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} B=(1,\infty ) \\  \\ \text{So,}A\cap B=(1,\infty )-N \\  \\ A\cup B\neq (1,\infty ) \\  \\ \Rightarrow S1\text{is only correct} \end{array}$

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{lllll} x_{i} & f_{i} & x_{i}^{2} & f_{i}x_{i} & f_{i}x_{i}^{2} \\ 2 & 4 & 4 & 8 & 16 \\ 4 & 4 & 16 & 16 & 64 \\ 6 & α & 36 & 6α & 36α \\ 8 & 15 & 64 & 120 & 960 \\ 10 & 8 & 100 & 80 & 800 \\ 12 & β & 144 & 12β & 144β \\ 14 & 4 & 196 & 56 & 784 \\ 16 & 5 & 256 & 80 & 1280 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Sigma f_{i}x_{i}^{2}=3904+36α+144β \end{array}$

Given, mean $=9$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Variance}=15.08 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{\Sigma f_{i}x_{i}^{2}}{\Sigma f_{i}}-\left (\dfrac{\Sigma f_{i}x_{i}}{\Sigma f_{i}}\right )^{2}=15.08 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{3904+36α+144β}{40+α+β}-(9)^{2}=15.08 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{3904+180α}{40+2α}=81+15.08[\because α=β] \\  \\ \Rightarrow 3904+180α=96.08(40+2α) \\  \\ \Rightarrow 3904+180α=3843.2+192.16α \\  \\ \Rightarrow 60.8=12.16α \\  \\ \Rightarrow α=5=β \\  \\ \therefore α^{2}+β^{2}-αβ=25+25-25=25 \end{array}$

text: Let the eccentricity of an ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ is reciprocal to that of the hyperbola $2x^{2}-2y^{2}=1$. If the ellipse intersects the hyperbola at right angles, then square of length of the latus-rectum of the ellipse is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Equation of hyperbola is $2x^{2}-2y^{2}=1$

$\Rightarrow \frac{x^{2}}{1/2}-\frac{y^{2}}{1/2}=1$

Here, $a=b$

$\therefore$ Eccentricity of rectangular hyperbola is $\sqrt{2}$

$\therefore$ Eccentricity of ellipse is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Since, ellipse intersects the hyperbola at right angles

$\therefore$ Ellipse and the hyperbola are confocal

$\therefore$ Foci of hyperbola $=(1,0)$

$\Rightarrow$ Foci of ellipse, $ae=1$

$\begin{array}{ll}  & \Rightarrow a\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )=1 \\  \\  & \Rightarrow a=\sqrt{2} \\  \\  & \therefore e^{2}=1-\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}} \\  \\  & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}=1-\frac{b^{2}}{2} \\  \\  & \Rightarrow \frac{b^{2}}{2}=\frac{1}{2} \\  \\  & \Rightarrow b^{2}=1 \end{array}$

$\therefore$ Length of the latus rectum $=\frac{2b^{2}}{a}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2}$

$\therefore$ Square of length of the latus rectum $=2$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text: The value of $\tan 9^{\circ }-\tan 27^{\circ }-\tan 63^{\circ }+\tan 81^{\circ }$ is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $\tan 81^{\circ }=\cot 9^{\circ }$ and $\tan 63^{\circ }=\cot 27^{\circ }$, the value is $(\tan 9^{\circ }+\cot 9^{\circ })-(\tan 27^{\circ }+\cot 27^{\circ })$.

As $\tan θ+\cot θ=\dfrac{\sin ^{2}θ+\cos ^{2}θ}{\sin θ\cos θ}=\dfrac{2}{\sin 2θ}$, the value is $\dfrac{2}{\sin 18^{\circ }}-\dfrac{2}{\sin 54^{\circ }}$.

With $\sin 18^{\circ }=\dfrac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}$ and $\sin 54^{\circ }=\cos 36^{\circ }=\dfrac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}$:

$\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{5}-1}-\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{5}+1}=\dfrac{8\left [\left (\sqrt{5}+1\right )-\left (\sqrt{5}-1\right )\right ]}{5-1}=\dfrac{16}{4}=4$

Hence, the answer is 4.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text: For $α,β,z\in \mathrm{ℂ}$ and $λ>1$, if $\sqrt{λ-1}$ is the radius of the circle $|z-α|^{2}+|z-β|^{2}=2λ$, then $|α-β|$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given equation of circle,

$\begin{array}{l} |z-α|^{2}+|z-β|^{2}=2λ \\  \\ \therefore 2λ=|α-β|^{2}.........(i) \end{array}$

For circle,

$|z-z_{1}|^{2}+|z-z_{2}|^{2}=|z_{1}-z_{2}|^{2}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Radius,}r=\frac{|z_{1}-z_{2}|}{2}=\frac{|α-β|}{2}=\sqrt{λ-1} \\  \\ \Rightarrow |α-β|=2\sqrt{λ-1} \\  \\ \Rightarrow |α-β|^{2}=4(λ-1) \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2λ=4(λ-1)[\because \text{Using Eq. (i)]} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2λ=4 \\  \\ \Rightarrow λ=2 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow |α-β|^{2}=4 \\  \\ \Rightarrow |α-β|=2 \end{array}$

text: If the lines $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{2-y}{-3}=\frac{z-3}{α}$ and $\frac{x-4}{5}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z}{β}$ intersect, then the magnitude of the minimum value of $8αβ$ is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, lines

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{2-y}{-3}=\dfrac{z-3}{α} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{3}=\dfrac{z-3}{α}=λ.........(i) \end{array}$

Any point on the line (i)

$x=2λ+1,y=3λ+2,z=αλ+3$

and line $\frac{x-4}{5}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z}{β}=μ$ ............(ii)

Any point on line (ii)

$\Rightarrow x=5μ+4,y=2μ+1,z=βμ$

Since, given lines intersect

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore 2λ+1=5μ+4..........(iii) \\  \\ 3λ+2=2μ+1............(iv) \\  \\ \text{and}αλ+3=βμ..........(v) \end{array}$

On solving (iii) and (iv), we get

$λ=-1,μ=-1$

On putting value of $λ$ and $μ$ in (v), we get

$\begin{array}{ll}  & α(-1)+3=-β \\  \\  & \Rightarrow α=β+3 \end{array}$

Now,

$\begin{array}{l} 8αβ=8(β+3)(β) \\  \\ =8\left (β^{2}+3β\right ) \\  \\ =8\left (β^{2}+3β+\dfrac{9}{4}-\dfrac{9}{4}\right ) \\  \\ =8\left \{\left (β+\dfrac{3}{2}\right )^{2}-\dfrac{9}{4}\right \} \end{array}$

$=8\left (β+\frac{3}{2}\right )^{2}-18$

Here, minimum value $=-18$

$\therefore$ Magnitude of the minimum value of $8αβ$ is 18 .

$\begin{array}{l} (20)^{19}+2(21)(20)^{18}+3(21)^{2}(20)^{17} \\ +\ldots \ldots +20(21)^{19}=k(20)^{19} \\  \\ \Rightarrow (20)^{19}\left [1+2\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )+3\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )^{2}+\ldots +20\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )^{19}\right ]=k(20)^{19} \\  \\ \Rightarrow k=1+2\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )+3\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )^{2}+\ldots +20\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )^{19}..........(i) \end{array}$

Now, 

$\begin{array}{ll} k\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )=\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right ) & +2\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )^{2}+3\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )^{3}+\ldots +20\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )^{20} \end{array}$ ........(ii)

On subtracting Equation (ii) from Equation (i), we get

$\begin{array}{l} k\left (\dfrac{-1}{20}\right )=1+\dfrac{21}{20}+\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )^{2}+\ldots \ldots +\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )^{19}-20\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )^{20} \\  \\ \Rightarrow k\left (\dfrac{-1}{20}\right )=\dfrac{1\left (\left (\frac{21}{20}\right )^{20}-1\right )}{\frac{21}{20}-1}-20\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )^{20} \\  \\ \Rightarrow k\left (\dfrac{-1}{20}\right )=20\left (\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )^{20}-1\right )-20\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )^{20} \\  \\ =20\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )^{20}-20-20\left (\dfrac{21}{20}\right )^{20} \\  \\ \Rightarrow k\left (\dfrac{-1}{20}\right )=-20 \\  \\ \Rightarrow k=400 \end{array}$

text: The number of points, where the curve $y=x^{5}-20x^{3}+50x+2$ crosses the $\mathrm{x}$-axis, is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given equation of curve

$\begin{array}{l} y=x^{5}-20x^{3}+50x+2 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx}=5x^{4}-60x^{2}+50 \end{array}$

On putting $\frac{dy}{dx}=0$

$\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow  & 5\left (x^{4}-12x^{2}+10\right )=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & x^{2}=\frac{12\pm \sqrt{144-40}}{2}=6\pm \sqrt{26} \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & x^{2}=6-\sqrt{26},6+\sqrt{26} \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & x^{2}=6-5.10,6+5.10 \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & x^{2}=09,11.1 \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & x=\pm \sqrt{0.9},\pm \sqrt{11.1} \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & x=-0.95,0.95,-3.33,3.33 \end{array}$

Now, 

$\begin{array}{ll} y(0) & =2(+\mathrm{ve})\Rightarrow y(1)=+\mathrm{ve} \\  \\ y(2) & =-\mathrm{ve}\Rightarrow y(3.3)=-\mathrm{ve} \\  \\ y(-1) & =-\mathrm{ve}\Rightarrow y(-2)=+\mathrm{ve} \\  \\ y(-3.3) & =-\mathrm{ve} \end{array}$


[IMG]


$\because \text{Required number of points}=5$
